title: stale cannot evaluate validity_conditions, so a lapsed condition is undetectable
description:
FINDING, made during T-399. This is the mechanical half of T-404.

precedent.py stale reports ONE check only: check=D [decay-candidate], citation decay, threshold
10 subsequent publications, 36 candidates across 59 records at the time of writing. It does not
read validity_conditions at all. Confirm that by reading the function before building anything.

CONSEQUENCE. Every tier-1 record in this layer states the conditions under which it stops being
valid, in prose, and NO TOOL IN THIS HARNESS CAN NOTICE WHEN ONE OF THEM STOPS HOLDING. T-404's
finding was made by a coordinator reading the record by hand while doing unrelated work. That is
not a detector.

WHAT TO BUILD, and the hard part is the honesty and not the code:
  A verb that lists each record's validity_conditions next to whatever the harness can actually
  measure about them, and that says plainly which ones it CANNOT evaluate.

The trap to refuse. A tool that pattern-matches prose and emits 'condition no longer holds' will
be wrong, and wrong in the expensive direction, because it would report a tier-1 record as
lapsed on a string match. Follow the currency.py precedent instead: emit the figure and refuse
the verdict. If a condition cannot be mechanically evaluated, the correct output names the
condition and prints NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE. A report listing 59 records as 'unknown' is a
TRUE report and is more useful than a false one, because it tells a reader exactly how much of
this layer rests on nobody having checked.

Registry rules that apply. GUARD-MENTION-C: if any test scans source for a token, parse the AST
instead, because prose explaining a command will trip a substring scan. This is the fourth time
that defect would apply. TELEMETRY-PROVENANCE-A: report counts raw AND distinct, never one.

Ship with the count of conditions in each bucket, and pin the bucketing with tests.
acceptance_criteria: Read the stale implementation first and record verbatim which checks it runs; the claim 'validity_conditions are not evaluated' must be evidenced, not assumed.
A verb that lists every record's validity_conditions and, per condition, either a measured value or the literal NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE.
NO pass/fail verdict on prose conditions. A false lapse report on a tier-1 record is the expensive failure; refuse the verdict as currency.py does.
Any test that inspects source parses the AST, never a substring scan (GUARD-MENTION-C, fourth occurrence).
T-404's finding appears in the output when the verb runs against the live registry: PR-022's condition is listed, and listed as one this tool cannot evaluate.
Full suite green; negative control run and reported for at least one test per group.

notes.note:
T-405 CERRADO con el verbo `precedent.py conditions`.

LA AFIRMACION DEL TITULO ES IMPRECISA Y SE CORRIGE. El criterio 1 pedia leer la
implementacion primero y registrar verbatim que revisa, y evidenciar la afirmacion en vez de
asumirla. Leida:

  check V   evalua SOLO las dos FORMAS mecanicamente checables (V1-35): `path:N-M` y una
            ruta pelada con prefijo `path:`. Una entrada que falla se vuelve hallazgo.
  V1-35     las entradas de texto libre las reporta `stale --json` como "unchecked": true,
            "never flagged, never an error", en sus propias palabras.
  check D   candidatos de decaimiento, que no tienen que ver con condiciones de validez.

Asi que stale SI evalua las formas checables y SI reporta las de prosa. EL HUECO ES A DONDE
VA ESE REPORTE. Medido contra el registro vivo el 2026-08-19:

  modo texto:  "stale: 34 reconsideration candidate(s) across 60 record(s)"
  --json:      64 entradas con "unchecked": true, las dos de PR-022 entre ellas

Quien corra el modo por omision ve un conteo limpio y no tiene ninguna senal de que 64
condiciones nunca fueron evaluadas. El verbo nuevo es esa vista faltante.

QUE EMITE. Por registro y por condicion: la forma (free-text / bare-path / file-line), y o
bien un VALOR MEDIDO o bien el literal NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE con su razon. Nunca los
dos. Un campo `holds` booleano solo para las checables; None para la prosa, siempre.

SIN VEREDICTO SOBRE PROSA, y la razon es el costo asimetrico. Un reporte falso de caducidad
sobre un registro de nivel 1 le entrega a quien quiera debilitarlo una razon generada por
maquina para tratarlo como vencido, y la clausula 4 de PR-022 es la restriccion mas fuerte de
la capa. currency.py fijo el precedente: emitir la cifra, rehusar el veredicto.

CONTEOS CRUDOS Y DISTINTOS (TELEMETRY-PROVENANCE-A), y la divergencia es el hallazgo, no un
artefacto: 113 crudas / 90 distintas en total, 66 crudas / 64 distintas no evaluables. Una
misma frase cargada por varios registros caduca en todos a la vez, y reportar solo el conteo
distinto esconderia a cuantos registros alcanza una sola caducidad.

RECONCILIA CONTRA stale. Se agrega la cifra solo-activos porque stale salta los registros no
activos: 64 crudas activas contra las 64 unchecked de stale --json, y una prueba lo verifica
contra el registro vivo. Sin esa cifra, una diferencia de alcance y un error se ven iguales
desde afuera.

EL HALLAZGO DE T-404 APARECE EN LA SALIDA (criterio 6): las dos condiciones de PR-022 se
listan y las dos quedan como NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE, con una prueba que fija el texto
exacto de la primera. Y el reporte dice, en su propia salida, que una condicion escrita como
afirmacion de hecho puede caducar EN LA LETRA sin caducar EN EL PROPOSITO, nombra a PR-022
como el ejemplo vivo y a T-404 como la pregunta de canon abierta, y declina resolverla.

SIEMPRE SALE 0. Es un REPORTE, no una revision; stale es la revision y ya es dueno del codigo
de salida de una condicion que falla. Una prueba AST fija que cmd_conditions no devuelve otra
cosa.

PRUEBAS: 19 nuevas en test_precedent_conditions.py, en cinco grupos, CON CONTROL NEGATIVO EN
CADA GRUPO donde el grupo lo admite (criterio 7):
  - la disposicion: que el literal no se estampa sobre todo, o la prueba principal pasaria
    sobre una herramienta que dejo de medir;
  - los conteos: que crudo y distinto de hecho difieren en algun caso, o el par seria adorno;
  - la negativa a juzgar: que el ayudante AST encuentra lo que si esta y levanta StopIteration
    con lo que no, o un parser que no empatara nada haria pasar todas las demas;
  - el registro vivo: que no todo el registro es prosa, o la afirmacion sobre PR-022 no
    probaria nada sobre el clasificador.
Toda prueba que inspecciona codigo PARSEA EL AST, nunca escanea subcadenas (GUARD-MENTION-C,
octava ocurrencia): los docstrings del modulo hablan largamente de veredictos y caducidades,
y un escaneo no distingue esa prosa de una asignacion.

Suite completa: 691 passed, 4 skipped.

VERIFIED. `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py conditions` (commit 439eed0,
.harness/bin/precedent.py) replayed independently against the live registry, plus one
synthetic adversarial fixture the producer's suite does not exercise.

(a) reconciliation against `stale --json`, exact match, replayed myself:
    `precedent.py conditions --json` -> not_evaluable_active_raw=64, not_evaluable_active_distinct=64
    `precedent.py stale --json` -> 64 entries with "unchecked": true (check=V), both of
    PR-022's condition strings among them. 64 == 64, matches the note's claim exactly.
    Also matched the note's other cited figures: records_raw=60, conditions_raw=113,
    conditions_distinct=90, not_evaluable_raw=66, not_evaluable_distinct=64,
    evaluable_raw=47/evaluable_distinct=26 (113=47+66, 90=26+64, consistent).

(b) no pass/fail verdict on prose anywhere in the live report: scripted a scan of every row
    in `conditions --json`'s `by_record[].conditions[]` -- 0 rows where form=="free-text"
    and holds is not None, and 0 rows where form=="free-text" and disposition is anything
    other than the literal "NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE". Also 0 rows where a checkable form
    (file-line/bare-path) was wrongly stamped NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE.

(c) PR-022's condition appears and is marked unevaluable: confirmed directly --
    `by_record` for PR-022 lists both conditions ("FORCE-IDENTITY-A is open: ..." and "no
    stored standing or balance field exists...") each with disposition "NOT MECHANICALLY
    EVALUABLE" and holds=null -- exact match to T-404's finding and the acceptance criterion.

(d) writes nothing: `find .harness/precedents -type f -exec shasum -a 256` before and after
    running `conditions` in both --json and text mode -- diff is empty (0 bytes different,
    0 files added/removed), and `git status --short .harness/precedents` shows nothing.

(e) always exits 0: text mode exit 0, --json mode exit 0, and on an EMPTY registry (a root
    with a bare `precedents/` dir and zero records, not in the producer's test suite) --
    also exit 0 with a clean all-zero report rather than a crash or nonzero.

Additional adversarial check (different angle from the producer's fixtures, which use only
string entries): fed `validity_report()` a record with a dict-shaped condition, an int, None
and an empty string as `validity_conditions` entries. All four were handled without a crash,
JSON-dumped into readable text, and correctly marked free-text/NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE
-- no exception, no silent drop. Also confirmed the active/non-active split is correct: a
second record set to status="superseded" contributed its unevaluable condition to
`not_evaluable_raw` but NOT to `not_evaluable_active_raw`, matching the documented
reconciliation-with-`stale` design (stale skips non-active records).

Tests: `python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_precedent_conditions.py -q` -> 19 passed.
Full suite: `python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q` -> 691 passed, 4 skipped (matches the
note's "691 passed, 4 skipped").

Cognitive diversity from producer: producer's evidence is the CLI/API output plus AST tests
within test_precedent_conditions.py; I independently replayed the CLI commands myself, wrote
a standalone reconciliation script comparing `conditions --json` against `stale --json`
byte-by-byte on the live registry, hashed the precedents directory before/after for the
no-write claim, and fed the report function a non-string/malformed-entry fixture the
producer's own test file never constructs.

All 7 acceptance criteria hold. Accepting.
